excerpt: Stream your movies, TV shows, and music from your own server.
description: Jellyfin is a free and open-source media server that organizes and streams your personal media library to virtually any device. It supports movies, TV shows, music, live TV, DVR, and user accounts without requiring a subscription.

excerpt: Manage all your indexers from one place.
description: Prowlarr centralizes indexer management for applications like Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, and Readarr. Configure your indexers once and automatically sync them across your media automation stack.

excerpt: A lightweight web interface for managing and viewing files.
description: Qui is a lightweight web application from the autobrr project that provides a simple interface for browsing and managing files through your browser.

excerpt: A lightweight BitTorrent client with a powerful web interface.
description: qBittorrent is an open-source BitTorrent client that provides fast downloads, RSS support, search plugins, bandwidth scheduling, and a modern web UI for managing torrents from anywhere.

excerpt: Monitor your system's performance in real time.
description: Glances is a cross-platform system monitoring tool that displays CPU, memory, disk, network, process, and container statistics through an intuitive web interface or terminal dashboard.

excerpt: Monitor your services and get notified when they go offline.
description: Uptime Kuma is a self-hosted uptime monitoring solution that checks the availability of websites, APIs, servers, and services. It includes status pages, notifications, and response time tracking.

excerpt: Host your own Minecraft server in minutes.
description: The itzg Minecraft Server container makes it easy to run a customizable Minecraft server with support for Vanilla, Paper, Spigot, Fabric, Forge, and more.

excerpt: Manage your Docker containers from an easy-to-use web interface.
description: Portainer is a lightweight management interface for Docker that lets you create, manage, monitor, and troubleshoot containers, images, networks, and volumes through a web browser.

excerpt: Easily manage reverse proxies, SSL certificates, and domain names.
description: Nginx Proxy Manager provides a simple web interface for managing Nginx reverse proxies and SSL certificates. It makes it easy to securely expose self-hosted applications using custom domain names and automatic Let's Encrypt certificates.

excerpt: Automatically update your running Docker containers.
description: Watchtower monitors your running Docker containers and automatically updates them when new images are available. It can help keep a homelab up to date without manually pulling new images and recreating containers.

excerpt: Monitor the uptime and availability of your services.
description: Uptime Kuma is a self-hosted monitoring tool that lets you monitor websites, servers, Docker containers, and other services. It supports HTTP, TCP, Ping, DNS, and other monitoring methods with notifications for downtime.

excerpt: Monitor your server's CPU, memory, disk, network, and system resources.
description: Glances is a cross-platform system monitoring tool that provides an overview of CPU, memory, disk, network, processes, and other system resources through a web interface.

excerpt: View and monitor Docker container logs in real time.
description: Dozzle is a lightweight web-based Docker container log viewer. It provides a simple interface for viewing and following logs from running containers in real time without needing to use the command line.

excerpt: Create a customizable dashboard for your homelab services.
description: Homepage is a highly customizable self-hosted dashboard for organizing and accessing your homelab services. It can display service status, system information, bookmarks, and integrations from a single web interface.

excerpt: Build a customizable dashboard for all your self-hosted services.
description: Dashy is a self-hosted dashboard that provides a customizable interface for organizing links and applications across your homelab. It supports icons, status checks, authentication, themes, and numerous integrations.

excerpt: Block ads and trackers across your entire network with DNS.
description: Pi-hole is a network-wide DNS sinkhole that blocks advertisements, trackers, and other unwanted domains for devices connected to your network. It also provides a web interface for viewing DNS activity and managing blocklists.

excerpt: Block ads and trackers with a network-wide DNS server.
description: AdGuard Home is a network-wide DNS server that blocks advertisements, trackers, and malicious domains. It provides detailed DNS statistics, filtering controls, and a web interface for managing your network's DNS traffic.

excerpt: Build your own private cloud for files, photos, calendars, and more.
description: Nextcloud is a self-hosted cloud platform that lets you store, sync, and share files across your devices. It also supports calendars, contacts, collaboration, file sharing, and a large ecosystem of additional applications.

excerpt: Synchronize files directly between your computers and devices.
description: Syncthing is an open-source continuous file synchronization tool that keeps files synchronized between computers and other devices without relying on a central cloud service.

excerpt: Manage your files through a simple web-based file browser.
description: File Browser provides a lightweight web interface for managing files and directories on your server. Users can upload, download, rename, move, delete, and organize files directly from a browser.

excerpt: Run your own S3-compatible object storage server.
description: MinIO is a high-performance, S3-compatible object storage server designed for self-hosted environments. It provides object storage for backups, applications, media, development environments, and other workloads that use the S3 API.

excerpt: Back up and organize your photos and videos on your own server.
description: Immich is a self-hosted photo and video management platform designed as a private alternative to services such as Google Photos. It provides automatic mobile backups, albums, search, sharing, facial recognition, and a modern web interface.

excerpt: Securely connect to your homelab from anywhere with a private mesh VPN.
description: Tailscale creates a secure private network between your devices using WireGuard. It makes it easy to remotely access servers, services, and other devices without exposing them directly to the public internet or configuring traditional port forwarding.

excerpt: Create a fast and secure VPN for remote access to your network.
description: WireGuard is a modern, lightweight VPN protocol that provides secure encrypted connections between devices. It can be used to remotely access your homelab, securely connect networks, or route internet traffic through your home server.

excerpt: Securely expose services to the internet without opening inbound ports.
description: Cloudflare Tunnel creates an encrypted connection between your homelab and Cloudflare, allowing you to securely publish web applications without directly exposing your server or opening inbound firewall ports.

excerpt: Add single sign-on and centralized authentication to your homelab.
description: Authentik is an open-source identity provider and authentication platform. It provides single sign-on, multi-factor authentication, user management, and access control for self-hosted applications.

excerpt: Protect your self-hosted applications with two-factor authentication.
description: Authelia is an open-source authentication and authorization server that works as a companion to reverse proxies. It can protect applications with single sign-on, two-factor authentication, access policies, and session management.

excerpt: Detect and block malicious activity targeting your services.
description: CrowdSec is an open-source security engine that analyzes logs and network activity to detect malicious behavior. It can identify attacks such as brute-force attempts and abusive traffic and share threat intelligence with other CrowdSec users.

excerpt: Run your own traditional OpenVPN server for remote network access.
description: OpenVPN is a widely supported VPN solution that allows remote devices to securely connect to your private network. It can provide encrypted access to homelab services and internal network resources from outside your home.

excerpt: Run large language models locally on your own hardware.
description: Ollama makes it easy to download and run large language models locally. It provides a simple API for interacting with models and can run models such as Llama, Mistral, Gemma, and other open-source AI models directly on your homelab hardware.

excerpt: Use your local AI models through a ChatGPT-style web interface.
description: Open WebUI is a self-hosted web interface for interacting with local and remote AI models. It provides a ChatGPT-style experience with conversations, model management, file uploads, document processing, and support for services such as Ollama.

excerpt: Create AI-generated images and workflows with a powerful node-based interface.
description: ComfyUI is a node-based interface for running generative AI workflows. It is commonly used for image generation, image-to-image workflows, video generation, and other AI-powered media tasks using models such as Stable Diffusion and Flux.

excerpt: Run an OpenAI-compatible AI API locally on your homelab.
description: LocalAI is a self-hosted AI inference platform that provides an OpenAI-compatible API for running language models, image generation, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and other AI workloads locally without relying on external cloud services.

excerpt: Convert speech and audio into text using OpenAI Whisper.
description: Whisper is an open-source automatic speech recognition model that converts spoken audio into text. It can be used for transcription, subtitles, voice notes, meeting recordings, and other speech-to-text workloads.

excerpt: Host your own lightweight Git repositories and development platform.
description: Gitea is a lightweight self-hosted Git service for managing repositories, issues, pull requests, releases, users, and collaboration. It provides a simple alternative to hosted Git platforms while keeping your source code on your own server.

excerpt: Run your own complete DevOps platform for source code and CI/CD.
description: GitLab Community Edition is a self-hosted DevOps platform that combines Git repositories, issue tracking, merge requests, CI/CD pipelines, container registries, security tools, and project management in one application.

excerpt: Run VS Code in your browser and develop directly on your server.
description: Code Server provides a browser-based version of Visual Studio Code that runs on your homelab. It allows you to write, edit, and run code remotely without installing a full development environment on your local computer.

excerpt: Automate builds, tests, deployments, and other development tasks.
description: Jenkins is an open-source automation server used to build, test, and deploy software. It can automatically run development workflows whenever code changes are pushed to a repository.

excerpt: Store and distribute your own private Docker container images.
description: Docker Registry is a private container image registry that lets you store, manage, and distribute Docker images from your own server. It is useful for homelabs and development environments that build and deploy their own container images.
